title: Nonuniform gap costs can overturn a unit-cost buffer placement
problem: For a fixed vessel order on one berth with endpoint-specific delay caps, determine whether the R02 minimum-total-buffer placement remains optimal when each idle gap has a different nonnegative linear cost.
failure: The R02 unit-cost placement [0,0,3] is feasible in the three-vessel witness but costs 30 at gap prices (1,10), while [0,3,0] costs 3. The first local certificate run also stopped before assertions due to a helper-call arity error. HORUS review then found that the initial finite certificate compared primal and dual values without asserting dual capacity feasibility.
correction: Formulate positive R02 interval demands as min c^T g subject to Mg>=w and g>=0. The dual packs valued intervals subject to each gap's price capacity. Consecutive-ones total unimodularity gives an integral primal optimum for integer demands. In the witness, assert both dual capacity constraints and matching primal/dual objective values; preserve and log the earlier harness failure.
transfer: Do not carry optimality across a change in the objective weights. Re-formulate the weighted objective, and check primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and matching values before using a primal-dual witness.
limits: One berth, fixed sequence, rectangular bounded arrival and handling uncertainty, endpoint-specific caps, and nonnegative linear per-gap costs. The executable certificate checks one three-vessel example and 43 bounded integer placements; it does not verify the general TU theorem or provide a general optimizer. Weighted buffer scheduling is established; the exact specialization's novelty remains unresolved. No operational data or human peer review.
author: TOTO
